scope.method: Close reading of full transcripts, original initial-code records/annotations/memos, consolidated excerpts, and every T1–T4 machine claim. Relations are qualitative judgments of defensible human meanings as a set; claim identifiers are provenance anchors, not a similarity score.

rows.explanation: Both identify the prolonged father–child separation, while the AI usefully retains its seven/eight-year duration.
rows.source_anchor: "My father, uh, immigrated to the United States when I was about eight months old... My mother and family were supposed to follow. And it took another eight years before we got there."

rows.explanation: The birthday and doll are a memorable first encounter with a changed social world, but AI does not claim this passage or meaning.
rows.source_anchor: "I had my first, eighth year, my first birthday party, at eight years, here in the States... we didn't celebrate birthday parties in Russia... here I had my first birthday party and my first doll."

rows.explanation: The dependent-citizenship relation is an explicit legal-historical meaning; no AI claim develops it.
rows.source_anchor: that was the last year that you became a natural citizen by virtue of your husband or your father being an American citizen.  And we automatically became citizens of the United States when we arrived

rows.explanation: Pogroms and repeated flight support both human pre-migration insecurity and the AI’s habitual-violence account.
rows.source_anchor: "The pogroms... became an everyday situation. Any number of times our whole family had to escape our home and run to Rizhon."

rows.explanation: The human code names childhood political upheaval; AI’s general memory theme does not make a claim about this takeover or its childhood significance.
rows.source_anchor: Well, my first memory, I had some nasty memories.  My first memory is, I must have been about four or five years old, and there was probably a Communist, or a revolutionary takeover

rows.explanation: A year in Warsaw awaiting cleared papers is a direct process barrier; AI’s separate arranged-passage claims do not represent this waiting experience.
rows.source_anchor: ...spent about a year in Warsaw till the papers were cleared and everything was set up for us to go.

rows.explanation: The killing, extortion, and child’s witness substantiate family violence/trauma and the AI violence claims.
rows.source_anchor: "Some Cossacks came and demanded money... They first killed him. They shot him... they made my grandmother come up with the money."

rows.explanation: All accounts recognize involuntary separation when the mother and grandmother are arrested.
rows.source_anchor: My mother and my grandmother were arrested, and the three of us were alone."

rows.explanation: The human insight is the child’s personal memory within a political event; AI captures pride and a red dress but not that contrast.
rows.source_anchor: there was a parade in the little village that we were in.  And my mother had made me a beautiful red dress, and I was in the parade on a wagon.  So I think that's the first historical moment that impresses me

rows.explanation: Repeated escape and hiding are a shared survival/displacement meaning.
rows.source_anchor: There was constant upheaval, because different armies would be going through, and all of a sudden we all had to desert our little town and run out and hide in the woods.

rows.explanation: Illness and the train-door injury directly support a physically difficult journey, but AI makes no claim about either; C1’s overlapping sickness excerpt is separately aligned at row 27.
rows.source_anchor: I was deathly sick all the way.  Um, somewhere along the line I think it must have been probably from Warsaw into Germany, but anyway a train hit my hand, a train door hit my hand, and I had a very bad situation there

rows.explanation: The threatened child’s near-abandonment supports both vulnerability and silencing through fear.
rows.source_anchor: My foot got stuck in the mud... they almost left me there... I cried out... somebody said, 'We're going to kill her if she doesn't shut up.

rows.explanation: Loss or sale of jewels and furs is plainly material/financial loss in transit.
rows.source_anchor: I remember that all my mother's jewels and furs were either taken or she sold them, and so when we got on the boat and I saw some women dressed beautifully I regretted that my mother didn't have her things any more.

rows.explanation: Her reflection explicitly joins ongoing action with fear made ordinary by repetition.
rows.source_anchor: When things happen on a regular basis... sure you're frightened all the time... but then you went right on. You didn't stop and think... You had to go on, and you did."

rows.explanation: The arrival scene supports hope, relief, and excitement as compatible facets of the same affect.
rows.source_anchor: Everyone pointing out the Statue of Liberty and 'we're here,' 'we made it,' and the excitement of everybody."

rows.explanation: The transcript explicitly calls the mother the household head; the AI preserves that family-authority insight.
rows.source_anchor: We lived with my grandfather and grandmother and my mother, who was more or less the head of the household.  There was also, uh, two uncles and an aunt still remaining in the home.

rows.explanation: The narrator’s own tentative account of her father’s motive supports better opportunity/economic pull.
rows.source_anchor: I imagine... he had gone here perhaps to find a better, easier way of life, and then he was going to bring his family here."

rows.explanation: Christmas, Santa, and wonder are a strongly supported new-cultural-experience reading.
rows.source_anchor: They were celebrating Christmas. I had never heard of Christmas... there was Santa Claus... all the beauty of Christmas suddenly hit me.

rows.explanation: Twelve families travelling at night supports collective, deliberately cautious migration, which AI does not take up.
rows.source_anchor: We packed food... twelve families... went by wagon, mostly by night so they wouldn't have any trouble."

rows.explanation: Pneumonia produces both a health barrier and forced maternal separation.
rows.source_anchor: Mother had... pneumonia... they questioned that... did not want to let her in the States. So they took her away."

rows.explanation: The blow and demand for buried money support a child-trauma reading alongside the AI’s granular violence account.
rows.source_anchor: I cried out, and somebody punched me in the jaw.  And then they made my grandmother come up with the money, which was buried, incidentally, in the backyard of the house

rows.explanation: Snow water, outdoor camp, and meals show transit conditions within a collective journey, absent from AI claims.
rows.source_anchor: We melted snow for water. We camped at night, we ate our meals.

rows.explanation: Her washing for her brother and stated pride support premature responsibility, not merely a task description.
rows.source_anchor: There was my brother and I, and we had to keep clean. I remember taking his wash and washing it... I felt so proud and grown up. I thought I was taking care of my brother."

rows.explanation: In its surrounding raid/pogrom context, the Jewish identity and targeted affluent household support ethnic persecution; AI makes the same contextual link, though motive remains cautious.
rows.source_anchor: my grandfather was a fairly affluent Jewish man in this little village.  He ran a mill.

rows.explanation: The human code captures unresolved traumatic sense-making; AI describes the raid’s sequence but does not retain the narrator’s unanswered question.
rows.source_anchor: Why would they come and kill him first and then ask for the money.

rows.explanation: First hot dog and banana, called revelations, substantiate discovery rather than a merely lexical food match.
rows.source_anchor: And they provided food for us.  I ate my first hot dog there.  I ate my first banana there and these were revelations.  You know, I'd never seen them, very exciting for this little kid.

rows.explanation: The repeated severe sickness supports physical difficulty, but AI makes no claim about the voyage illness; it is the overlapping C1 segment distinct from row 11’s injury passage.
rows.source_anchor: I was deathly sick all the way... I was very, very sick on the boat."

rows.explanation: The unexplained tag, rumors, and isolation jointly support bureaucratic uncertainty and fear.
rows.source_anchor: They put an identification tag on me... Maybe it means they're sending me back... Maybe it means they're sending me to my father... The stories... frightened this poor little kid to death.

rows.explanation: The speaker herself links educational interruption to inadequate background; AI captures the durable educational consequence.
rows.source_anchor: I've always regretted it... I never really learned how to study... I dropped out of high school... because we had an inadequate background.

rows.explanation: Being nearly left on the road is direct childhood vulnerability in a survival flight.
rows.source_anchor: I had an incident where I was running with my brother and family and uncles and, being the youngest in the family, my foot got stuck in the mud and they almost left me there and, because nobody wanted to be caught in the road.  Somehow they pulled me out.  The shoe remained.

rows.explanation: A settled father with a specialty deli supports both economic stability and an opportunity-oriented reading.
rows.source_anchor: Father was living here... He was pretty well established here by then... he had this... delicatessen."

rows.explanation: Depression, debt, and a reduced livelihood substantiate post-settlement economic hardship.
rows.source_anchor: We hit a Depression... My Dad... was happy to have [a newspaper stand] so that he could just manage to bring home bread.

rows.explanation: The sequenced relatives’ moves provide direct evidence of chain migration.
rows.source_anchor: actually there was an uncle that married into our family.  Um, who had been here first.  Came back and married an aunt of mine.  And they came back to the States.  And then my father and two of my mother's sisters left for the States, and then the war broke out

rows.explanation: House, garden, servants’ quarters, and the narrator’s assessment support pre-migration prosperity.
rows.source_anchor: As I said, my grandfather was in a fairly good position and we had this, it was a clay house, but it was a nice house with, at that time they had ovens to do their cooking and baking in, and above the oven was a loft where some of us slept.  They had their little garden and they had servants quarters there, so there must have been, it must have been pretty good.

rows.explanation: Relatives’ visit and reassurance are concrete kin support amid detention.
rows.source_anchor: We did have some relatives in New York... they reassured me that nothing like that was going to happen.

rows.explanation: Separation in chaos, injury, and eventual recovery support the human code and AI’s violence/memory account.
rows.source_anchor: I remember running away, too.  So that had to be, I think, after my grandfather was killed.  And I was climbing, there was a big mountain, a sand kind of mountain, dunes of some sort, where the most, the greater part of the village was peopled.  And, um, I remember running up there, being run over by a horse's hoof.  Climbing up to whatever home it was, and crying out a couple of times, and somebody said, "I think I hear a child crying," and somebody else said, "No, it's a dog."  And eventually they took me in and my family found me there the next morning.  Uh, so mostly really my memories are of a lot of upheaval and running away and because this, I seem to have been born about that time.

rows.explanation: Her stated happiness at being beside her brother makes comfort in family a supported meaning, absent from AI’s separation-focused claims.
rows.source_anchor: Eventually I landed in the next bed to my brother... it was great having the measles so I could be with him.

rows.explanation: The disguised father is an unmistakable reunion, with non-recognition as a meaningful detail.
rows.source_anchor: He pretended to be a doctor... Eventually he broke down and told us that it was him.

rows.explanation: Rapid advancement from first to eighth grade supports educational opportunity, with the later costs retained elsewhere.
rows.source_anchor: We were enrolled in school... In two or three years I was in eighth grade

rows.explanation: This is the same reunion event; AI’s claim preserves the father’s institutional workaround.
rows.source_anchor: and a man came to see us, what we thought was a new doctor.  My father.  It was my dad.

rows.explanation: The speaker explicitly frames her account as fragmentary and mediated by relatives’ stories, an AI-only contribution the human coding also attends to.
rows.source_anchor: Um, I wish I could tell you some more interesting things.  I tried, I need my aunt and my uncle, because they remembered so many beautiful things of Russia itself.  Uh, I just didn't remember my experiences, really.  Politically, it was rough all the way.

rows.explanation: Danish clustering to keep customs is a direct community-seeking and network claim.
rows.source_anchor: Uh, here in America it was because the Danes liked to settle in an area where they could be together and keep their Danish customs.

rows.explanation: The walnut episode is both a sensory first and an excited child’s voyage experience.
rows.source_anchor: The sailor... filled my skirt with these wonderful walnuts. I'd never eaten a walnut, so I thought that was really something."

rows.explanation: Anticipation and skyline support arrival excitement/expectation; AI adds only grounded scene detail.
rows.source_anchor: That was with great anticipation... vaguely the skyline as we came in... there were so many people."

rows.explanation: AI explicitly records the child volunteering and imitating examinations, supporting both procedure/health and C2’s playful agency.
rows.source_anchor: They all had to have some kind of examination... looked into people's eyes... between their fingers

rows.explanation: The narrator explicitly attributes lasting claustrophobic fear to the journey.
rows.source_anchor: I’ve never since been able to be in a close place because I’m afraid I’ll get smothered.

rows.explanation: The first ice-cream cone is a clear new-experience claim.
rows.source_anchor: That was our first ice cream cone.

rows.explanation: Non-transferable furniture skills and blueprint work substantiate occupational adaptation and rebuilding.
rows.source_anchor: In America people didn’t have their furniture made and there was no, there was no place for his skills in that line.  But he had also learned all about making blueprints and so one, you know

rows.explanation: Trying to walk back to Denmark directly supports homesickness, longing, and possible loneliness.
rows.source_anchor: I remember I wanted to go back to Denmark... we were on our way to Denmark.

rows.explanation: AI explicitly links the all-Danish social circle to initial lack of English, supporting community, language acquisition, and early school barrier readings.
rows.source_anchor: All the people we got together with were Danish and they spoke Danish.

rows.explanation: Waiting for a sibling’s birth before departure is a family-timed migration decision, which AI records.
rows.source_anchor: We came to the United States in 1912... We waited for my brother Carl to be born.

rows.explanation: Church, home practice, and retrospective value support preservation and bilingualism.
rows.source_anchor: Um, there was a Danish church and, of course, that was all Danish.  The sermons were Danish, the songs were Danish.  Everything was Danish.  Even when I was confirmed, that happens when a young person is 14 years old, that also was in Danish although by that time we, of course, all spoke English.  But, uh, my parents, well, they didn’t tell us we had to speak Danish at home.  It just came naturally.  We did.  And we’re glad now

rows.explanation: “America fever” is direct migration aspiration, though the AI appropriately avoids treating it as a fully specified economic motive.
rows.source_anchor: Then we moved into this house and then the America fever hit him. And then, of course we came to America.

rows.explanation: The balanced appraisal of South Dakota as a good childhood place despite climate is a human settlement evaluation absent from AI claims.
rows.source_anchor: It was very cold... very hot... but there were a lot of good things about growing up in South Dakota.

rows.explanation: Economic scarcity and glowing America stories explicitly establish push and pull.
rows.source_anchor: Times were really tough in Denmark... economics... it was hard to get ahead... they heard all these glowing stories of streets in America..."

rows.explanation: AI identifies both the California move and the college president’s invitation, supporting relocation and educational opportunity.
rows.source_anchor: We came out mainly because of Atterdag College... and then, of course, we stayed here.

rows.explanation: The broader ship sequence is not crosswalk-linked, but AI’s local children’s-journey theme explicitly captures self-directed curiosity, crew familiarity, and protection on this voyage.
rows.source_anchor: It was very interesting on that ship... there was so much to see."

rows.explanation: Compulsory Canadian routing and crowded family travel support both difficulty and bureaucratic inefficiency.
rows.source_anchor: My father... discovered that they sent us all the way up through Canada... it must have been really hard to travel with three little girls and a baby."

rows.explanation: The contractor career and visible built landscape substantiate post-migration economic achievement.
rows.source_anchor: My father... was a general contractor... the countryside there is dotted with his barns and houses

rows.explanation: Initial non-English schooling and six-month literacy support language barrier and acquisition together.
rows.source_anchor: I couldn't speak a word of English when I started school... after six months I could understand, speak and read English."

rows.explanation: The speaker explicitly calls bilingualism an advantage and a basis for belonging in both places.
rows.source_anchor: We did [speak Danish at home]... it's such an advantage to know both languages... when you go to Denmark you're just as at home."

rows.explanation: Temporary lodging with an uncle is direct receiving-family support.
rows.source_anchor: Then we got to South Dakota where my uncle lived with him for a couple of weeks or so until we could find a house to move into, until my father could get a house built for us.

rows.explanation: AI explicitly notes her Solvang shop and its thirty-one-year duration, supporting the human achievement code.
rows.source_anchor: Eventually I opened my shop... I had that for 31 years.

rows.explanation: Uncles’ pooled funds, visas, and aid to 23 people support kin-backed migration and procedural barriers.
rows.source_anchor: The two uncles... put together a quarter of a million dollars... brought out twenty-three people from Europe... some of them had to live in Poland until we could get a visa to come here.

rows.explanation: Religious observance shapes work and occupation while visa waiting creates a process barrier; both readings are grounded.
rows.source_anchor: And when the uncles sent for our family he was very perturbed because it meant he was going to have to work on Saturday, which was impossible, as far as he was concerned.  so when we went to Poland waiting for our visa, he, because of his Jewish education, he decided that he would be a schochet.   .

rows.explanation: Merchandise lost when a driver departs supports both loss and betrayal in transit.
rows.source_anchor: They brought a lot of merchandise... the driver... drove off with lots and lots of things

rows.explanation: The father’s anticipation and family’s Statue of Liberty viewing substantiate arrival wonder.
rows.source_anchor: Well, my father, too, was so excited that he couldn't wait.  So he wrapped us in blankets and took us up on deck, and we looked at the Statue of Liberty.

rows.explanation: AI records the infant’s fever, removal without explanation, and the mother’s repeated description of three terrible days; the absence was a crosswalk error.
rows.source_anchor: They took him from my mother... she had no idea what was going to happen... she spent three terrible days.

rows.explanation: Union exclusion directly forces relocation and is a concrete employment barrier.
rows.source_anchor: The union would not permit my father... so we had to move away from my mother's family

rows.explanation: The child’s English learning while the parent lacks it supports a language barrier and child-as-bridge reading.
rows.source_anchor: I spoke Yiddish and Russian, but I didn't speak English... I stayed there until I learned the language.

rows.explanation: Learning English through a neighboring woman is grounded social support and boundary-crossing.
rows.source_anchor: My mother became very friendly with a woman next door... she was learning English from this woman

rows.explanation: AI directly describes low earnings, failed Detroit income expectation, and the mother’s economic management, supporting the human settlement reading.
rows.source_anchor: We moved to Detroit... my father never really earned much money

rows.explanation: Working through school is direct evidence of education as upward mobility.
rows.source_anchor: We never knew how we would be able to do it, but we did it... worked our way through school

rows.explanation: Being different because of Orthodox practice supports religious social difference; language is secondary at most.
rows.source_anchor: I had the additional problem that I was different because my family was so Orthodox

rows.explanation: Cossack conscription pressure and a son’s departure ground flight as a migration motivation.
rows.source_anchor: When the Cossacks came... both sons were to be conscripted into the army... my grandfather sent the oldest son.

rows.explanation: Maids, education, and explicit comfort support pre-migration prosperity.
rows.source_anchor: They had maids... they were fairly well educated... they lived a relatively comfortable life.

rows.explanation: Expected pogrom and attic hiding provide direct fear-before-migration evidence.
rows.source_anchor: When I was an infant... the Cossacks were coming... there was going to be a pogrom... they hid in the attic.

rows.explanation: Jewish exclusion from school and household teachers support education despite exclusion.
rows.source_anchor: He wanted them to be educated, but sending children to school if you were Jewish was very hard to do.  So he used to get a melamud [ph] or a teacher, who came to live in the house with them, and taught the children.  So when they learned all that teacher had to teach them, they would get a new one.  And my father ended up speaking six languages

rows.explanation: The mother’s excitement at sighting the Statue provides direct arrival expectation evidence.
rows.source_anchor: My mother was so excited... they had sighted the Statue of Liberty.

rows.explanation: Hiding from conscription before a delayed migration supports hiding to survive.
rows.source_anchor: his younger brother was the next one that the army wanted.  So I understand he hid out in various places before they were able to get him to America.  He came to America maybe five to ten years later

rows.explanation: The funds and 23 assisted migrants are strong evidence of collective financial rescue.
rows.source_anchor: And these two uncles, who had done very well, in fact the older uncle owned one of the largest drug stores in Pittsburgh at that time, put together a quarter of a million dollars, which just blows my mind because where they got that kind of money I don't know .  And brought out twenty-three people from Europe.

rows.explanation: Housing and salary through a religious community support settlement opportunity and community enablement.
rows.source_anchor: They will give you a house and a salary... my father loved the idea... we moved to Ann Arbor

rows.explanation: A later Russian contact facilitating college is a concrete diaspora-network resource missed by AI.
rows.source_anchor: I later, many, many years later, ran into somebody who knew them, from Russia, and helped me be able to go to college

rows.explanation: The contrast between limited income and both children’s college education supports education over wealth.
rows.source_anchor: He ended up teaching children and being a schoichet, and never making a lot of money, but both of us went to college.

rows.explanation: The infant’s cry, attic hiding, and family’s retrospective account support this unusual but transcript-grounded rescue meaning.
rows.source_anchor: And I started to cry, and they were so frightened that they would all be killed, and so they went up into the attic and pulled like a ladder that went up into the ceiling.  And the Cossacks came, and they had managed to calm me down before they got there.  And they feel, they felt that I, as a baby, saved the family,

rows.explanation: The broad statement that language was always a problem supports the human code and AI theme.
rows.source_anchor: There was always the language problem

rows.explanation: AI explicitly identifies the anti-Jewish beating as both violence and an enclave-boundary failure; the crosswalk false negative should not erase this match.
rows.source_anchor: My brother... was beat up... because he was Jewish

rows.explanation: AI recognizes the teaching career but reads it through an economically ascending Jewish community; the human code keeps the speaker’s aspiration and enjoyment in view.
rows.source_anchor: I always wanted to be a teacher... I always did very well in school." I loved teaching... I loved what I did

rows.explanation: AI explicitly identifies later descendants’ reconnection in California, supporting the human diaspora-family-reconnection code.
rows.source_anchor: The cousins have become very, very friendly... we've formed very close friendships.

rows.explanation: Writing bar-mitzvah speeches because of the father’s English limits is strong child-language-bridge evidence.
rows.source_anchor: And when I was ten, I used to write their bar mitzvah speeches because my father's English, although his Hebrew was wonderful, his English was not good enough to help them.  So I wrote bar mitzvah speeches

rows.explanation: AI records the father’s teaching and the daughter’s bar-mitzvah language role, but does not make the narrator’s present work with children into the human intergenerational-vocation insight.
rows.source_anchor: I now go to the synagogue, and I hear boys being, or girls being bar mitzvah, and I still know the maftir by heart because I heard it so many times as I was growing up.  And I think I'm still doing what my father was doing, because I now work with children with learning problems on a one-to-one basis.

rows.explanation: AI recognizes university graduation as the result of children’s work, but the human code retains her specific academic rank and self-described achievement.
rows.source_anchor: I was very proud of myself.  I always did very well in school.  When I graduated from the university, I was in children's literature, which was being taught as a separate subject.  And I graduate third in my group because you were placed in a job according to where you were on this list

rows.explanation: The passage’s repeated love of teaching supports occupational fulfilment, an unclaimed human insight.
rows.source_anchor: I taught, I loved it from the very first day.  It was the most wonderful thing.  I could do, I just loved turning children on.  I did very well during my student teaching

rows.explanation: Ongoing contact and students’ outcomes support impactful contribution, although this lies beyond core migration themes.
rows.source_anchor: And many of these gifted children, I still keep contact with.  One of them is in Canada now doing research in diabetes.  She has her own laboratory, paid for by the Canadian government.  One of my former, many of my former students are, the girls are mechanical engineers and doctors and lawyers and, in fact, when they had their tenth year reunion, they invited my husband and me to come as their guest, and it was so exciting seeing these kids that I had helped train, and what they had achieved.  The young woman who had invited me said that was the best part of the reunion for her, because when she said, "Mrs. Turkin is here," everybody was so thrilled.

rows.explanation: Bad or scarce work and the search for a better life directly ground migration motivation.
rows.source_anchor: The work was bad... There wasn't much work.

rows.explanation: The playful, non-seasick voyage is a positive journey account not captured by AI’s aligned claims.
rows.source_anchor: Oh, I just remember running around out there... Having fun. We didn't get too seasick.

rows.explanation: The unfamiliar ice-cream cone clearly supports first cultural encounter/discovery; community support is not evidenced in this short excerpt.
rows.source_anchor: It was kind of strange... the first thing I ate... was a Tootie Fruity ice cream cone.

rows.explanation: Peer mockery of speech directly supports language-based discrimination, while “got over it” qualifies its duration.
rows.source_anchor: The kids used to make fun of us talking, but we got over that after a while.

rows.explanation: The speaker explicitly maps ethnic neighborhoods and clannish coexistence, supporting community/enclave codes.
rows.source_anchor: In the east side, where we lived, was a whole bunch of Scotch people and then, like on the south side there was a lot of Slavic and, you know, Polish and what else was there?  Just, you know, the Slavic people in another end of town, and they were all kind of clannish, you know.  But they got along, but they were kind of clannish.

rows.explanation: Clan meetings, dance, and bagpipes directly support cultural preservation.
rows.source_anchor: We belonged to a Scottish clan... meetings... dances... bagpipes... Scottish dancing

rows.explanation: Maintained contact with dispersed club peers substantiates continuing ethnic-community connection.
rows.source_anchor: You still keep in contact with those girls that you, the Balmoral Club…. Oh yeah. Sure. Uh-huh. … You still keep in contact with at least half a dozen of them, or more. … Yeah. They're scattered now.

rows.explanation: Lost contact and uncertainty about relatives support severed homeland connections.
rows.source_anchor: I had cousins and relatives back there, but I don't know. I haven't contacted them for, oh, since I was real little, so I don't know if they're still living or not.

rows.explanation: Work deterioration and a wider Scottish flow support economic migration.
rows.source_anchor: The work got bad. So he came over... There were a lot of Scotch people that came over at that time

rows.explanation: AI explicitly identifies the father’s year-earlier departure as family separation and establishment before the family followed; this is a crosswalk false negative.
rows.source_anchor: My father came a year before... my mother and sister and I came the next year.

rows.explanation: Making evening entertainment during the crossing supports a positive journey experience missing from AI coverage.
rows.source_anchor: We used to dance... at the things they had at night... We made our own entertainment

rows.explanation: Threatened retention at Ellis Island and release through lodging costs support procedure/arbitrary detention.
rows.source_anchor: They wanted to keep us over there... my mother told us they'd have to pay for our hotel... so they let us go

rows.explanation: The father’s boarding arrangement and first shared lodging provide a grounded settlement account.
rows.source_anchor: Of course my father was living... boarding with someone... we stayed there until we found a place of our own."

rows.explanation: A “regular Scotch colony” directly supports ethnic-community support and AI’s network interpretation.
rows.source_anchor: We had a regular Scotch colony over there

rows.explanation: Keeping to one’s own before work broadened contacts supports a staged social-integration account.
rows.source_anchor: You kept to your own, until I grew up and went to work.

rows.explanation: Post-arrival friendship formation supports community support, with AI’s institution-building interpretation remaining grounded.
rows.source_anchor: Everybody just sort of met there after they came. Just made friends
